title: Seven Years, a 7-Acre City, and Nawazuddin as the Villain. Tumbbad 2 Is Coming — and Sohum Shah Wants You to Wait for It.
excerpt: The cult folk-horror that became India's most beloved slow burn is finally getting its sequel. The catch: you won't see it until December 2027.
body:
There is a particular kind of patience that only Tumbbad fans understand. They waited six years for the original to find them — a 2018 folk-horror that flopped quietly, then crept through word of mouth until a 2024 re-release made it the second highest-grossing re-released Indian film in history, crossing Rs 20 crore on day ten alone. Now they are being asked to wait again. And judging by the reverent hush around Sohum Shah's latest update, they will.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=kFCfsDOu2go

This week the actor-producer posted a thoughtful note about the seven-year road to Tumbbad 2, and industry insiders filled in the rest: a sequel this deliberate doesn't get rushed to feed a content calendar. It gets built. Literally. A massive set sprawling across seven to eight acres has risen in Mumbai, designed to resemble a full-scale colonial city — the kind of immersive, rain-blackened world the first film carved into the imagination of anyone who saw it.

"Tumbbad has always been very special to me, and with Tumbbad 2, the idea is to take that world forward in a way that feels deeper and more expansive." — Sohum Shah

That ambition has a price tag in days. The team is mounting a shoot expected to run more than 200 days, an almost unheard-of schedule in an industry that increasingly shoots films in six weeks and prays. It signals something the original earned the hard way: Tumbbad is not a franchise to be milked. It's a mythology to be honored.

**""When Sohum shared the vision for the sequel, I liked the story and joined them on their journey."

Details of his character remain locked behind closed doors, which is exactly how this team likes it."**

The man who plays the dark

The casting coup is Nawazuddin Siddiqui, stepping in as the antagonist — a piece of news that, on its own, reframes the entire project. Few actors can hold menace the way Nawaz can hold a silence, and dropping him into Tumbbad's universe of greed, curses, and the insatiable god Hastar feels less like a casting choice than a dare.

!Mumbai — Photo: Wikimedia Commons

"Tumbbad has always been a film I admired for its originality and atmospheric storytelling," Siddiqui said of signing on. "When Sohum shared the vision for the sequel, I liked the story and joined them on their journey."

Details of his character remain locked behind closed doors, which is exactly how this team likes it. The makers have teased only a single, ominous phrase — Pralay aayega. The deluge is coming. After what Hastar did to audiences in the first film, that's all the warning anyone needs.

The rumor mill, meanwhile, has been working overtime. Whispers have linked everyone from Alia Bhatt to Priyanka Chopra, Katrina Kaif, and Nayanthara to the project, with the loudest chatter suggesting Alia could take on a key role. The makers have stayed silent — which, in Bollywood, only makes the speculation louder.

The pedigree behind the puja

Tumbbad 2 went on floors in April with a mahurat ceremony that doubled as a statement of intent. Producers Dr. Jayantilal Gada and son Dhaval Gada of Pen Studios — the powerhouse behind RRR and Gangubai Kathiawadi — were there, alongside industry stalwarts Boney Kapoor and Tutu Sharma. The film is co-produced under Shah's own Sohum Shah Films banner, with Adesh Prasad, co-director of the original, now taking the directorial reins in collaboration with Shah. (Rahi Anil Barve, who directed the 2018 film, is not at the helm this time.)

"Tumbbad 2 is envisioned as a grander cinematic experience," Gada said, "with a story that deepens the universe while keeping audiences thoroughly engaged."

For the diaspora: mark the calendar in pencil

Here is the part that will test NRI patience: the global theatrical release is locked for December 3, 2027. That's a long horizon for diaspora fans in the US, UK, and Canada who discovered the first Tumbbad on streaming and have been evangelizing it at every dinner party since. The original is currently available to stream in most markets, and a rewatch is practically mandatory homework — the sequel is being built to reward those who remember every frame of Hastar's curse.

Is eighteen months a long time to wait for a horror film? For any other franchise, maybe. For Tumbbad — the film that taught a generation that greed is the only monster that never dies — it's barely a held breath. They built the cult on patience. They're betting it holds.
